problems.description: Regression from patch 59: a tsrs loop that the loop model misses is never recovered. Since 59, any overdue request the model does not flag is forgotten. The looping tsrs worker then spins for the rest of the session. Each repeat of the request (the editor asking again at the same position) is sent again and takes another worker. After a few of these, tsrs answers nothing and no restart ever happens. 7179942 recovered with one restart. The model misses any loop whose walk passes a regex literal containing a quote, `//` or `/*`, because tsgo_loop's tokenizer has no regex literals. In `/'/` the `'` opens a string to the end of the line. In `/\/*/` the `/*` opens a comment to the next `*/` or the end of the file, which hides every later line.
problems.fix:
(a) tsgo_loop.rs, Tokens::new: before the `//` and `/*` checks, scan a regex literal wherever a `/` cannot be division:
- regex when there is no previous token or it is Other, Open, Comma, TypePunctuation, Reserved, LessThan or GreaterThan;
- division after Word, Literal or Close.
Read to the closing `/`, honouring `\` escapes and `[...]` classes, stop at a line end, then skip the flags. Emit it as a token the walk stops at. Add the probed texts to tests/data/tsrs-lost-requests.json.
(b) Add a safety net that does not depend on the model. Keep an overdue completion or signatureHelp the model does not flag tracked as suspected instead of forgetting it. tsrs answers a slow one even after cancellation (slowsig on 8c8c100 logs `response to unknown tsgo request 3`); it never answers a looping one. While a suspect is outstanding on a document, hold back further completion and signatureHelp there, as patch 62 does. Restart, with RestartBackoff and never while a pull of its document is with tsgo, when either:
- the suspect is still unanswered after about 4 timeouts, or
- another request times out while it is outstanding.
Robustness tests: a fake tsgo that ignores an unflagged completion and lets a hover time out must restart; slow-but-answering requests must not.

problems.description: Pre-existing, still broken: renaming an imported component leaves its closing tags, so the file no longer parses. svelte2tsx's port writes `</Name>` as one overwrite (`{spaces}{slot_close}{name}}`, inline_component.rs), so the name maps to the `<`, two characters early. 7179942 applied the off-by-two edit and garbled the text; patch 63 now drops it, which leaves mismatched tags.
problems.evidence:
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hyprsonic-Developer-hyprsonic-uk--experiments-zeno/957f62ce-c5e3-468e-b125-e60c604064fd/scratchpad/rev6/mine/cases/component.json, run with rn.mjs.
- Renaming `Child` to `Kid`: 8c8c100 gives `<Kid kind="a">text</Child>` and `<Kid kind="b">…</Child>`. References report the closing tags as zero-width `5:20-5:20` and `9:33-9:33`.
- Renaming the namespace `UI` to `Lib`: 8c8c100 gives `<Lib.Box>{n}</UI.Box>`.
- 7179942 gives `textKidld>` (edit `5:20-5:25` over `</Chi`) and `{n}LibUI.Box>`.
- Official 0.18.5 gives `</Kid>` and `</Lib.Box>`.
problems.fix: Projection: in handle_inline_component's closing-tag branch, overwrite `closing_tag_start..closing_tag_start+2` and `name_end..comp.end` and leave the name in place (or `insert_copy` the name range), so the name maps exactly and the code stays byte-identical. Language server fallback in rewrite_workspace_edit: when the mapped source text is `</` followed by the generated name, shift the range by two instead of dropping the edit. Test: rename a component and a namespaced component that have closing tags.

problems.evidence:
Cases in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hyprsonic-Developer-hyprsonic-uk--experiments-zeno/957f62ce-c5e3-468e-b125-e60c604064fd/scratchpad/rev6/mine/cases (template.json, component.json, multiline.json); results for 8c8c100, 7179942 and official are in ../res.
- Renaming snippet `cell` from `{@render cell(n)}` edits only the render sites and leaves `{#snippet cell(x: number)}` (reference `7:0-7:0`). Renaming at the declaration returns no edit.
- Renaming `Size` leaves `{#snippet cell(x: Size, …)}`, `inner(y: Size)` and `named(q: Size)` inside `<Child>` (references `12:0-12:0`, `13:0-13:0`, `18:18-18:18`).
- Renaming `Row` misses `r: Row`.
- Renaming `id` misses the each key `(row.id)` (reference `10:11-10:11`).
- Renaming `active` or `color` leaves `class:active` and `style:color` (reference `14:44-14:44`).
- Official 0.18.5 renames all of these.
- 7179942 corrupted them instead (`rowippet`, `Dimippet`, `{onclickonunt}`).

problems.description: Pre-existing rename corruption: renaming a variable used in a `bind:` shorthand rewrites the directive's property name instead of expanding the shorthand. correct_shorthand only handles a tsgo `public: value` pair, and tsgo returns a plain name here.
problems.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hyprsonic-Developer-hyprsonic-uk--experiments-zeno/957f62ce-c5e3-468e-b125-e60c604064fd/scratchpad/rev6/mine/cases/shorthand.json: renaming `let value = $state("")` used in `<input bind:value />` to `text`. 8c8c100 and 7179942 both give `<input bind:text />` (edit `13:12-13:17 text`), which binds a property inputs do not have. Official gives `<input bind:value={text} />`.
problems.fix: In tsgo_rename.rs correct_shorthand: when the source range directly follows `bind:` (and `class:` or `style:` once those are mapped), is followed by whitespace, `/` or `>`, and the replacement is a plain identifier, return `{old}={{{new}}}` over the same range. Test: `<input bind:value />` rename.

problems.description: Pre-existing: renaming a store from a `$store` use drops the `$` prefix, so uses read and write the store object instead of its value.
problems.evidence: shorthand.json query at `{$count}`, renaming to `total`. 8c8c100 (same as 7179942) gives `const total = writable(0)`, `function onclick() { total++; }`, `{total}` and `{#if total > 1}`. Official gives `$total` at every use. Renaming from the declaration works, but its references list only the declaration, while official lists the three `$count` uses.
problems.fix: In the store bridge (collect_generated_followups and the rewrite of `$name` occurrences), when an edit replaces a source `$name` while renaming the store `name`, emit `$` + newName, or narrow the range to after the `$`. Add the `$name` uses to references the same way. Test both rename positions.

problems.description: Minor regression from patch 65: in a component whose `$$ComponentProps` alias stays inside `$$render` (a generic component, or an annotation using `typeof` of a local), a half-typed type literal above the props declaration loses its TypeScript errors. Only Svelte's own parse error remains. The errors sit in the copy's generated prefix (`;type $$ComponentProps =  `), which is now neither the old approximate token nor an exact segment, and they are dropped.
problems.fix: Map a diagnostic that starts in an insert_copy prefix to the copy's start (the annotation), as the source map already does, instead of dropping it as generated. Test with the TypeOpenGen and TypeOpenTypeof texts.

problems.description: Pre-existing, related to the documented unmapped repaired alias: when script recovery repairs a half-typed props annotation, the alias stays plain text mapped to 0:1. The recovery's placeholder then produces semantic errors on the `<script` tag; patch 43 only drops syntax errors there.
problems.evidence:
diag2.json, same output on 245dbfb and 8c8c100:
- `let { a }: { a: string; b: } = $props();` gives ts 2304 "Cannot find name '_'" at 0:1;
- `{ a: Array<string }` gives ts 2314 "Generic type 'Array<T>' requires 1 type argument(s)" at 0:1.
Official gives 1110 'Type expected' at 1:28 and 1005 at 1:30.
problems.fix:
When props_alias_copy declines because the text was repaired, either:
- still emit the alias as an insert_copy of the original annotation range with the recovery fill as the copy's suffix, so it maps to the annotation; or
- wrap the repaired alias in Ωignore markers, so its diagnostics are dropped (Svelte's parse error already reports the half-typed annotation).
Test with both texts.

notes:
I didn't edit vendor/rsvelte or the svelte-rs repo and didn't commit anything. Tools and results are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-hyprsonic-Developer-hyprsonic-uk--experiments-zeno/957f62ce-c5e3-468e-b125-e60c604064fd/scratchpad/rev6: tools/ (copies of tests/regressions), mine/ (rn.mjs, diagcmp.mjs, missedloop.mjs, pullwhileloop.mjs, cases/, res/), model/ (tsgo_loop.rs harness and probes), fuzz/ (lsfuzz2 output) and corpus/. Load average was 30–45 throughout, so timings are noisy; the restart, edit and diagnostic results are not.

**Issue A is fixed.** On 8c8c100 (sha1 0d7a691):
- propsrename: edits 1:6, 3:23 and 2:8, line 0 intact, line 3 `{ kind: Dim }`; references are the same three ranges.
- hashrename: Card's rename is `Size as Dim` at 1:15, plus 1:50, 1:70 and 2:23. Nothing lands at 0:1 and there are no duplicate edits.
- genericsrename, generics (1109, 1139 and 1005 inside the value) and propsfeatures match the integration record.

**Extra rename checks, against official svelte-language-server 0.18.5 as oracle.** Rename, references, definition and highlights match official for:
- props with defaults, `$bindable` and rest;
- an `interface Props` reference, and an intersection with an interface;
- module-script types used across components;
- a `typeof` local (alias inside `$$render`);
- non-destructured props and a multi-line annotation with comments;
- a rename from a .ts file into a Svelte annotation;
- generics with `>` inside the value, multi-line, unquoted, single-quoted, and with a module-script constraint type;
- CRLF and non-ASCII lines.

Every 7179942 edit that 8c8c100 no longer returns was a corrupt edit (its source text was not the renamed name). Patches 55, 56 and 63 dropped no correct edit in any case I ran.

**Generated code is byte-identical.** I generated 400 components (351 with the `$$ComponentProps` alias, 320 generic renders, combining module scripts, imports, hoisted types, snippets, `typeof` locals and a props declaration as the first statement). 245dbfb and 8c8c100 project all 401 shadows identically.

**Issue B is fixed for slow requests.** With a 3 s timeout:
- slowsig, 6 aliases, signature and definition: answered at 5 s, no restart, TS2322 at 7 s.
- slowmix: no restart, the pull returns at 7.25 s.

At the default timeout, slowsig with 36 aliases answers `null` at 32 s, no restart, and TS2322 arrives at 42 s (7179942: 76 s). tsrs's late answer to the cancelled signature help does arrive.

**Real loops still recover.**
- loopstorm: 3 restarts with the backoff, hovers answered in 1–2 ms.
- pullwhileloop (my script): pulls of the looping document every 1.5 s are each answered at once with their 186 TS diagnostics. The restart follows the timeout, so the pull rule cannot deadlock.

**lsfuzz2, seeds 1–40 × 300:**
- No panic, no unanswered request, no duplicate or unknown response.
- Seeds 12, 22, 30, 36 and 37 hit a real tsrs loop. Each was flagged and recovered with one restart, and tsgo never answered any of those requests late.
- Seeds 30 and 36 report final-diagnostic mismatches against a fresh server, both after the restart, on documents whose final text has no `lang="ts"`. This looks like an artifact of the comparison: the restarted tsgo reopens the buffer as JavaScript (the fuzz side shows 8016 'Type assertion expressions can only be used in TypeScript files'), while the fresh server keeps the first language id, which lsfuzz2's own comment says tsgo does.

**Verdict.** Problem 1 is the only clear regression that matters: a loop the model misses turned from one restart into a permanent outage. It needs the regex tokenizer fix and the safety net before or soon after shipping. Problems 2–5 and 7 are pre-existing; patches 55 and 63 turned their corruption into silently incomplete renames. Problem 6 is a minor diagnostic loss from patch 65.

Not reported as problems:
- A module script ending in a half-typed `import {` in front of a generic instance script gets '=>' expected at the generics closing quote. Official reports the same error at the same place.
- In a multi-package workspace, renaming from a .ts buffer edits only that file. 7179942 does the same, and Zed does not route .ts files to this server.
